Documentation / Developer / Startup architecture

Startup architecture

Perastage creates an application-owned startup::Metrics context at the start of OnInit. The context follows configuration setup, window construction, startup-path resolution, project loading, and the final UI commit. MainWindow exists as the application top window but remains hidden while the splash owns the visible startup experience.

Restore phases

  1. Resolve the explicit platform/command-line request or last-project fallback.
  2. Traverse the project package and restore scene.mvr, configuration, resources and optional layout-cache entries.
  3. Resolve the saved view preset and active project layout.
  4. Resolve the semantic viewport requirement from the saved view mode and lazily construct that viewport before loading the AUI perspective. Legacy perspectives are inspected only when no recognized semantic mode exists.
  5. Populate project tables and layers from the authoritative scene.
  6. Apply the saved AUI perspective and activate the saved project layout.
  7. Refresh visible summaries and rigging data and perform the final AUI update.
  8. Maximize and show MainWindow with its authoritative layout under an update lock. Queue a continuation for show/maximize sizing and shell publication, commit final sizes, and publish native child controls once. For a visible 3D view, retain the splash until all source resources have completed and a natural scene paint has presented them with input enabled. Only then emit InteractiveReady and dismiss the splash; optional navigation representations may continue preparing.
  9. Schedule non-essential fixture-symbol preparation.

The UI thread owns wxWidgets controls, AUI perspective commits, viewport creation and OpenGL contexts. Background services may prepare immutable symbol inputs after InteractiveReady; their existing project epoch checks prevent a result from being published into a replacement project.

InteractiveReady

InteractiveReady is emitted once from the queued splash completion pass. The initial idle pass shows the previously hidden MainWindow under an update lock. It queues a CallAfter continuation to resolve final native sizes, commit AUI/layout, and explicitly refresh and update native control subtrees to establish the native shell boundary. For visible 3D startup, an observer of normal viewer paint events queues a readiness check after the renderer has returned. Splash dismissal requires source loading to finish, a scene presentation, an enabled frame/viewer and no viewport interaction lock. It does not wait for optional navigation representations. Completion does not require another idle event: ongoing progressive viewport activity can delay idle delivery after the frame becomes visible. Showing the frame alone is not treated as completion of native painting. The readiness check uses the read-only HasPendingSourceResourceLoading() query, including resource synchronization not yet initialized, rather than status text or a progress percentage. It never requests a scene paint or synchronizes resources. The queued observer also records a scene presentation preceding shell publication, so empty projects do not require another paint just to close the splash. At that point the authoritative scene and configuration are loaded, the saved view and active layout are selected, required panes exist, visible project panels have current data, and no startup callback remains that will replace the layout. Deferred external opens remain queued and are processed after this boundary.

Project cache transfer

The primary ProjectSession ZIP traversal captures bounded entries below resources/layout_view_cache/ in a typed archive-resource payload. The layout viewer clears stale state and consumes that payload. Cache parsing and deep source validation remain optional and non-fatal; cache failure cannot affect scene or configuration restore. The normal load path never reopens the .pstg to acquire this cache.

The version 6 Layout cache is raster-first. A matching bounded RGBA snapshot is independent of the optional command-replay payload, so a view whose replay graph exceeds 75,000 commands still saves its final raster. Command counting stops as soon as the limit is exceeded. Individual raster resources are capped at 8 MiB and the transferred Layout raster set is capped at 16 MiB; malformed dimensions and byte counts are rejected without affecting authoritative project loading.

The startup cache also retains the final legend raster. Hydrated view and legend snapshots upload directly to the Layout Viewer context without requiring the scene capture panel. Legacy schema versions are non-authoritative and are safely rebuilt. When a cold render needs legend symbols, the captured snapshot is published to every matching legend cache before the incremental renderer can return after another element, preventing duplicate capture on the next tick.

Version 6 validation binds cache metadata to the exact serialized scene.mvr bytes and the sorted names and exact bytes of packaged Layout images. Both use the fnv1a64-v1 contract. Save computes these identities from buffers already owned by the export/resource pipeline; load updates them while the primary ZIP traversal reads either the bounded scene buffer or spill file. A fully covered match takes the fast path and never calls the extracted-source deep hasher. Schema 5 and incomplete-coverage caches retain conservative deep validation.

Legend persistence hashes the logical GDTF specification, mode, fixture type, visible row settings and presentation values. Runtime symbol lookup continues to use the resolved workspace path, but temporary mvr-import-* paths never enter the persistent legend identity. Raster cache metadata is scoped to a versioned Windows, macOS or Linux wxWidgets rendering contract so disposable pixels are not reused across incompatible font/rendering environments.

The first active Layout rebuild uses a minimal event-loop yield rather than the 180 ms interactive-edit debounce. Queue wait and event-loop overrun are measured from the actual request and dispatch boundaries. Warm raster painting no longer constructs the offscreen Viewer2D renderer; capture resources are acquired only when the requested view cannot be served by its exact persistent raster.

For Layout-mode startup, automatic fixture-symbol inspection is released by the Layout render-ready event rather than immediately after InteractiveReady. Candidate inspection then advances one fixture per idle slice, keeping paint, timer and input events ahead of non-essential post-startup scanning.

Project archive sources

The primary .pstg traversal now captures config.json into an owned byte payload and patches packaged layout-image paths before the configuration store applies it. The normal path therefore performs one JSON parse and does not create a temporary configuration file. Standalone JSON loading remains a thin file wrapper over the same byte parser.

scene.mvr uses a bounded archive-source policy. Entries up to 128 MiB are read into one owned buffer and passed to MvrImporter; larger entries spill to the existing project temporary directory as they are read. The limit is named at the ProjectSession API and can be reduced by deterministic tests. It is conservative enough for normal projects while preventing archive metadata from causing an unbounded allocation. The importer wraps either the file or memory source in the same wxInputStream extraction implementation, including the same traversal and case-collision checks. It continues to extract the inner MVR workspace because GDTF and model consumers still require stable paths.

The startup record distinguishes memory restores, spill fallbacks, spill bytes, configuration memory loads, and configuration patch time. Normal bounded projects have one .pstg traversal, one scene-buffer restore, no project-level scene/config temporary write, and retain only the required inner MVR resource workspace. Spill files remain solely for scenes exceeding the memory policy.

Deferred GDTF fingerprint validation

Automatic fixture-symbol preparation no longer invalidates semantic fingerprints at read sites. Capture records both the memoized semantic fingerprint and the cheap path/size/modification-time revision. Publication reuses the captured fingerprint when both revisions are available and equal; otherwise it performs the conservative semantic revalidation and rejects stale work as before. GDTF writers remain responsible for invalidating or publishing the cache at their existing mutation boundaries.

Profiling

Diagnostic logs and the internal CMD panel receive the stable StartupProfile event=InteractiveReady summary. It reports measured bootstrap phase durations; project archive open, traversal, scene extraction, cache transfer and MVR restore values; layout and AUI commits; viewport ensures and constructions; and authoritative table/layer reloads. A second diagnostic-log record identifies post-startup fixture-symbol scan scheduling. This boundary measures the selected-view presentation boundary, not compositor completion or completion of optional progressive navigation/quality representations.

Reusable project panels use an explicit initial-population policy. MainWindow requests deferred population so startup data is built once after project load; standalone construction defaults to immediate population. Layout2DViewDialog keeps its existing first-show layer reload and therefore also requests deferred construction.

Standard view modes

Saved project restore and manual standard-view selection are separate flows. A saved perspective retains compatible project-specific docking and panel visibility, while the required central pane and all five main toolbars are enforced. The manual 3D, 2D, and Layout commands use explicit pane visibility and docking recipes rather than perspectives captured from mutable runtime state. This makes transitions history-independent even when a heavyweight viewport is constructed for the first time after Layout Mode.

GUI publication during File → Open

Archive parsing, project restoration, and resource processing retain their existing paths. After a successful archive restore, a scoped wxWindowUpdateLocker holds the visible frame through saved-layout selection, table/layer reloads and summary/rigging refreshes. The separate modal progress dialog remains live; progress updates can dispatch events without publishing partially rebuilt frame controls. Its auto-hide terminal value is reserved for the final GUI publication call, because archive sub-stages can each report a completed range before GUI composition begins. Status messages continue to be recorded. An archive-load failure occurs before this lock; an exception or early exit inside the composition scope automatically thaws the frame.

Saved-layout application configures newly required viewport panes, perspective, visibility, docking and minimum sizes before its AUI commit. Interactive viewport construction and manual preset commands retain their own commits. Summary captions defer their AUI commit while the frame is frozen; the final project-load AUI/layout/size commit includes them.

At the publication boundary the frame thaws and native GUI subtrees are refreshed/updated once before completing the progress dialog's auto-hide range and releasing the load disabler. PublishNativeGuiChildren excludes GL canvases and any ancestor containing one, including Inspector preview canvases. Before exposing controls, native erase backgrounds are initialized from the active system theme: content controls use the window colour and shell controls use the button-face colour. Explicit colours (such as Console's black background) are preserved. Initialization also excludes GL-containing subtrees and is applied to initially hidden native controls so that later activation has the same background. It does not change scene clear colours or render resources. MSW Update() only paints the target HWND, so wx child controls are also updated. GTK can recursively refresh/update native children, which is why simply calling MainWindow::Update() would be unsafe for this purpose. No platform specific branch, new yield, timer, sleep, or resource-completion threshold is used. Shell painting, structural readiness, and progressive scene completion remain separate boundaries. The Viewer3D 12 ms work budget, 128-resource batch limit and 150 ms presentation cadence are unchanged.

Manual visual regression procedure

Use STG MAHOU or another very large project on Windows, Linux and macOS. Save and repeat each scenario with 2D, 3D, Layout Mode and Inspector presets:

  1. Restore the project as the last project at startup. Confirm the splash stays visible through composition and the interface appears in its final docking positions with populated fixture, truss, layer, summary and rigging controls.
  2. Open the project through File → Open while another project is already open. Confirm progress continues and no empty/white controls or intermediate pane positions are exposed during reconstruction.
  3. Cancel the file chooser, then attempt to open an invalid project archive. Confirm the frame remains enabled, repainting and usable after failure.
  4. With 3D visible, confirm optional representations can continue preparing after the startup splash disappears. File → Open may also keep loading source resources after its project dialog disappears; status reporting remains live. For 3D startup specifically, the splash must remain through “Loading scene: …” and may close at “Preparing scene for navigation: …” after source geometry has been presented. Check orbit, pan, wheel zoom and keyboard camera actions after closure. The visible viewer must be enabled, interaction unlocked, and keyboard focus restored to it. Optional representations use the original source mesh until ready; dense scenes may navigate less smoothly until proxies finish. A populated shell must not retain the splash solely because optional navigation representations are still being prepared.

Native shell publication excludes the viewports. Startup separately waits for source-resource completion and a natural scene paint, but not for optional navigation/quality preparation. Neither boundary synchronizes resources or requests extra viewport frames. Where diagnostics are available, compare the same project and preset before/after for resource synchronization count, scene paint count and load duration. Separate the one-time native control publication cost from ongoing scene rendering.

2D regression smoke

A consumed 2D paint clears its repaint-coalescing flags even while loading has disabled interaction. Re-enabling the viewport queues one presentation; wheel and table-selection updates must not depend on switching view modes. Controller selection remains authoritative after picking, project loading and history replay.

After a Linux Ninja build with compile commands enabled, run xvfb-run -a python3 tests/run_viewport_regression_smoke.py build/wsl-x64-debug (or use the current desktop display). This optional native smoke reuses the application objects and creates its own synthetic PSTG and isolated app-data directory. It checks actual pane visibility on two saved-2D launches, project opening, wheel input, picking, selection pixels, view switching, label Apply/Close, Undo/Redo and save/reload. Cross-platform CI retains the normal lifecycle, composition, history and publication tests.
